successCriteria.description: The LeaveBalance entity exposes exactly the canonical field set — id, employeeId, leaveTypeCode, periodStart, periodEnd, entitledDays, usedDays, pendingDays — and no status field.
The balance service grants the FULL policy entitlement at the start of each accrual period: entitledDays equals the policy's annualEntitlementDays with no pro-rata reduction.
On period close, the service carries forward exactly min(unused, carryForwardDays) into the next OPEN period, where unused = entitledDays - usedDays - pendingDays; days above the cap are forfeited.
Jest unit tests under tests/unit/modules/balance/ cover both accrual (full entitlement at period start) and carry-forward (hard cap, forfeiture above cap) with in-memory fake repositories.

The public index.ts re-exports the model, repository interface, repository implementation, service interface, and service implementation so downstream modules (validation, leave) can import LeaveBalance and the balance service through the entry point only.

constraints: All database access goes through the repository layer (GP-001); the service never imports a pool, client, or module-level db helper.

The service owns the unit of work via an injected IUnitOfWork.withTransaction; participating repository/service methods take an optional trailing PoolClient and fall back to the shared pool when omitted. BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK are issued only by PgUnitOfWork, never by the balance repository.

LeaveTypeCode is imported from src/shared/types/index.ts (lowercase persisted values: annual, sick, emergency, unpaid, maternity, paternity); carryForwardDays is read from LeavePolicy in src/modules/policy/index.ts. No new enum or duplicate type is declared locally.
Errors are thrown as the shared typed errors from src/shared/errors/index.ts (ValidationError/NotFoundError/ConflictError), never as bare Error or inline status codes.

The module follows the established split-file convention (model, repository.interface, repository, service.interface, service, index.ts) matching employee/leave-type/policy/audit/notification, rather than the single-file layout listed in the task.
The Pg repository generates ids via randomUUID(), maps snake_case rows to camelCase via a mapRow helper, and accepts an optional trailing PoolClient.
No `any` (use unknown + type guards), no direct DB access outside the repository, no hardcoded secrets, no @gestalt/* dependencies.
outOfScope: Routes, controllers, and RBAC guards for the balance module — deferred to later phases; this phase delivers model/repository/service/index only.
Audit-log writes (GP-002) for balance state changes — audit is a separate module and not wired into balance in this phase.

The sufficiency check (entitledDays - usedDays - pendingDays >= requestedDays) and the requestedDays day-count helper — owned by the validation module (Phase 5) and shared/types respectively, not re-derived here.
Knex migrations / DDL for the leave_balances table — the code agent generates migrations as part of persistence work, not a deliverable of this phase's module files.

entityInvariants.invariant: A LeaveBalance row is uniquely identified per employee + leaveTypeCode + accrual period (periodStart/periodEnd); there is at most one balance row per (employeeId, leaveTypeCode, periodStart, periodEnd).
entitledDays, usedDays, and pendingDays are non-negative numbers, and usedDays + pendingDays never exceeds entitledDays for a given balance row.

periodStart is strictly before periodEnd; the accrual period boundaries are derived from the policy's accrualPeriodMonths and are contiguous (the next period's periodStart equals the prior period's periodEnd).
The entity has no status field; OPEN vs CLOSED is inferred from periodStart/periodEnd relative to the current date, not stored on the entity.

interfaceConstraints.operation: accrue / open period (grant entitlement at period start)
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Rejects invalid input (unknown leaveTypeCode, non-positive entitlement, invalid period range) with ValidationError; unknown employee/policy with NotFoundError; a duplicate balance for the same employee/type/period with ConflictError.

Carries forward exactly min(unused, carryForwardDays) into the next OPEN period and forfeits the remainder; throws NotFoundError when the source balance or target policy is missing, and ValidationError when the period is not closable.

interfaceConstraints.operation: read balance (retrieve by employee + leave type + period)
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns the matching balance or null/NotFoundError when none exists; never mutates counters.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: LeaveTypeCode must be the enum from src/shared/types/index.ts with lowercase persisted values (annual, sick, emergency, unpaid, maternity, paternity) — no local re-declaration.
carryForwardDays and annualEntitlementDays must be read from the LeavePolicy entity exported by the policy module's public entry point, matching its field names and types.
Error types must be the shared AppError subclasses (ValidationError 400, NotFoundError 404, ConflictError 409) with their stable code strings.
The repository must use the shared pg Pool from connection.ts (default pool) and follow the same mapRow/randomUUID/optional-PoolClient pattern as the existing PgLeaveTypeRepository.
The transaction boundary must match the IUnitOfWork.withTransaction contract (service owns the boundary, data-access opens it; optional trailing PoolClient on participating methods).

integrationPoints.why: LeaveTypeCode enum is the canonical leave-type discriminator used in the balance entity and service.
LeavePolicy supplies annualEntitlementDays (full entitlement) and carryForwardDays (hard cap) that drive accrual and carry-forward.
Typed error contract for validation/not-found/conflict semantics across the service.
Shared pg Pool is the default data source for the PgLeaveBalanceRepository.
LeaveType existence may be validated when opening a balance period for a leave type code.
